sources.title: Rahul Gandhi: historical party biography and presidency
sources.findings: Read Congress’s historical biography: birth 19 June 1970 to Rajiv and Sonia Gandhi; Rollins undergraduate degree in 1994 and Cambridge MPhil in 1995; consulting work before politics; first election in Amethi in 2004; AICC general secretary on 24 September 2007; vice-president in January 2013; party president from 16 December 2017. Its four-term/Wayanad current-office wording is outdated and replaced with PRS and parliamentary records. The May 2019 resignation shorthand is distinguished from the 3 July public letter. Bharat Jodo Yatra ran from 7 September 2022 to 30 January 2023. Organisational growth, social benefits and party claims of success are not independent findings; exact march length and participation totals are omitted.

sources.title: 18th Lok Sabha: Rahul Gandhi, Rae Bareli and parliamentary role
sources.findings: Read PRS’s 18th Lok Sabha profile: elected Congress MP for Rae Bareli, Uttar Pradesh, fifth term, term start 9 June 2024, current Leader of Opposition. Parliamentary activity coverage ends 13 August 2026, not the crawl date. The page explains that the opposition leader does not sign the attendance register, so N/A is not absence or zero attendance. PRS is an independent legislative-research organisation, not the parliamentary secretariat. Current office is also corroborated by November reporting. Party membership counts shown in navigation are not reused as certified election results.

sources.title: Cambridge confirms 1995 MPhil in Development Studies, 29 April 2009
sources.findings: Read the 29 April 2009 agency report in The Indian Express describing Cambridge Vice-Chancellor Alison Richard’s confirmation: Trinity College attendance October 1994–July 1995 and MPhil in Development Studies awarded in 1995. This is reporting of a university confirmation, not an original degree certificate or directly inspected university letter. The degree is not a PhD, and attendance at Harvard does not establish a Harvard degree. No unsupported degree subject for the Rollins bachelor’s qualification is added.

sources.title: Rahul Gandhi publicly announces resignation as Congress president, 3 July 2019
sources.findings: Read Xinhua report of 3 July 2019: Gandhi publicly released his resignation letter and accepted political responsibility for the general-election loss. A 25 May resignation offer had been rejected by party colleagues. The report also confirms losing Amethi and winning Wayanad in the same election. The timeline dates publication of the letter, not a separately certified party-committee acceptance or successor’s installation. Resigning as party leader was not resignation from Parliament. Electoral defeat is not treated as proof of every criticism of his leadership.

sources.publisher: Supreme Court of India; order reproduced by LiveLaw
sources.title: Rahul Gandhi v Purnesh Ishwarbhai Modi: interim order of 4 August 2023
sources.findings: Read the Supreme Court’s 4 August 2023 order as reproduced in LiveLaw’s PDF, including operative paragraphs 10–13 rather than only its editorial headnote. The Court stayed the conviction during the appeal; it did not decide the merits or acquit him. It discussed the lack of reasons for imposing the maximum two-year sentence and consequences for representation, while also criticising the remarks. The reproduced text/headnote uses 1950 for the Representation of the People Act; the official parliamentary notification cites 1951, so the profile avoids repeating the apparent year error. No current disposition of every later proceeding is inferred.

sources.publisher: Lok Sabha Secretariat / Gazette of India
sources.title: S.O. 3512(E): disqualification ceases to operate, 7 August 2023
sources.findings: Read Gazette S.O. 3512(E), dated 7 August 2023: Supreme Court relief on 4 August concerned the Surat trial judgment of 23 March, and disqualification notified on 24 March ceased to operate subject to further judicial pronouncements. This is parliamentary restoration following a stay of conviction, not final acquittal, an expunged trial history, or a finding about unrelated litigation. The exact original disqualification notice was referenced by this official notification rather than independently opened.

sources.publisher: Lok Sabha Secretariat / Gazette of India
sources.title: S.O. 2457(E): recognition as Leader of Opposition, 26 June 2024; effective 9 June
sources.findings: Read Gazette S.O. 2457(E), dated 26 June 2024: the Speaker recognised Rahul Gandhi, Congress leader in the Lok Sabha, as Leader of Opposition with effect from 9 June 2024 under section 2 of the 1977 statute. The effective date is separate from the June party announcement, the 26 June notification and the 27 June announcement in the House. This office is not Speaker, prime minister or Congress president.

sources.title: 18th Lok Sabha first-session resume: Wayanad resignation, pages 11–12
sources.findings: Read relevant sections of the Lok Sabha Secretariat’s September 2024 resume of the 18th Lok Sabha first session, especially printed pages 11–12: Wayanad seat resignation effective and accepted on 18 June 2024, announced in the House on 24 June. The later Speaker-announcement table records opposition-leader recognition on 27 June. Session dates were 24 June–2 July; those dates do not replace effective appointment dates. The full publication’s unrelated tables were not audited, and no claim that he now represents both Wayanad and Rae Bareli is made.

sources.title: Hyderabad Bharat Summit speech and platform-worker activities, 14 November 2026; reported 15 November
sources.findings: Read Indian Express report updated 15 November 2026 describing the Saturday, 14 November Bharat Summit speech in Hyderabad and platform-worker activities that day. It establishes an actual speech, not merely an advertised event. Assertions about electoral manipulation, business influence, democracy and future electoral victory remain Gandhi’s political claims. No independent voter-roll analysis, criminal finding, verified insurance payout or completed national policy is inferred. Embedded media were not watched. The party event page corroborates the date and title but did not expose a complete transcript.

sources.title: Columbia University remarks and BJP response, 18 November 2026
sources.findings: Read Times of India report updated 18 November 2026 describing his Tuesday Columbia University appearance, hence 17 November, and employment/education remarks. It also reports the BJP’s rebuttal; neither side’s political characterization is adopted as an independent economic finding. The closing reference to a scheduled Chicago event calls 18 November Tuesday, although the calendar date is Wednesday. No Chicago attendance or future outcome is inferred from this inconsistent scheduling sentence. No full event video or university transcript was reviewed.

sources.title: Rahul Gandhi’s education and work before entering politics, 19 June 2023
sources.findings: Read relevant body paragraphs of The Indian Express’s 19 June 2023 education and pre-politics explainer, despite subscription-interface text elsewhere on the response. It corroborates Rollins graduation in 1994, Cambridge MPhil in 1995, Harvard attendance without graduation, Monitor Group work and first Amethi election in 2004. Its discussion of citizenship controversy is not evidence of British nationality; the profile makes no such claim. A linked Rollins alumni listing and original company filings were not separately inspected. No private school or degree records examined.
